title: Comparative phytochemical-assisted synthesis of ZnO@zeolite nanocomposites for multifunctional environmental and antibacterial applications
content: The integration of green-synthesized semiconductor nanoparticles with porous solid hosts has emerged as an effective approach to develop sustainable, multifunctional hybrid materials. The aim of this work was to biosynthesize zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles using the leaf extracts of Pilea peperomioides and Eragrostis tenella and then immobilize these ZnO nanoparticles on zeolite SGU-29 to form ZnO@zeolite nanocomposites. The effect of various phytochemicals from plants on the structural properties and functional performance of the nanocomposites was systematically studied. The synthesized materials were characterized by FT-IR spectroscopy, XRD, SEM-EDX, and thermogravimetric analysis to confirm the successful immobilization of the well-dispersed ZnO nanoparticles on the zeolite framework and the enhancement of the structural stability of the synthesized materials. The photocatalytic activity of the nanocomposites for the degradation of methylene blue was higher than that of pure ZnO. For the degradation of 1 ppm of dye, under optimized conditions (3 mg catalyst, pH 9), the Eragrostis tenella-derived ZnO@zeolite showed the highest degradation efficiency of 92.6%, and the Pilea peperomioides-derived ZnO@zeolite showed a degradation efficiency of 89.8% under alkaline conditions. In addition, the Eragrostis tenella-derived nanocomposite exhibited greater antibacterial properties against both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus with an inhibition zone of ∼19 mm and ∼17 mm, respectively, and maintained excellent photocatalytic stability for four reuses. The results indicate that the use of plant phytochemistry can be beneficial for optimizing the physicochemical properties and multifunctional performance of ZnO@zeolite nanocomposites for eco-friendly applications such as wastewater treatment and antimicrobial activity.
